paragraphs.text: DSH tools that drive your running Brave browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol
# dsh-plugin-brave-cdp

Drive **your own, already-running Brave** over the Chrome DevTools Protocol: the
real window, your p

rofile, your cookies, your logins, your tabs — including the
tab you are looking at right now.

Most browser automation launches a fresh browser it owns. This one attaches to the
one you already h

ave open, so an agent can read a login-walled page, fill a form in
a session you are signed into, or

hand a task back to you mid-flight in the same
window. Nothing is scraped from a parallel profile.
Two surfaces, one implementation:
| Surface | Use it when |
| **DSH tools** (`brave_tabs`, `brave_goto`, …) | an agent drives the browser — schemas, rendered re

sults, no shell quoting |
| **`brave-cdp` CLI** (shipped in this package) | a human or script drives
it, or you want `jq`/`batch` pipelines |
Both call the same CDP client, so behaviour and failure messages match.
## Tools
| Tool | Does |

| `brave_tabs` | list / open / focus / close tabs |
| `brave_goto` | navigate a tab (or a new one) a

nd wait for load |
| `brave_snapshot` | interactive elements with `@eN` refs (role, name, value, hre

f, state) |
| `brave_click` | real mouse click by `@eN` ref, CSS selector, or visible text |
| `brav

e_fill` | set an input / textarea / contenteditable, firing `input`/`change` |
| `brave_key` | press

a key, optionally with ctrl / shift / alt / meta |
| `brave_eval` | evaluate JavaScript in the page

, awaiting promises |
| `brave_wait` | wait for a selector, text, url, or document load |
| `brave_s
creenshot` | capture a PNG and return its path |

With no `tab` argument a tool acts on the tab the user is looking at
(`document.visibilityState ===

'visible'`), and every result carries the CLI's
`tab:` header so it is clear which tab ran the call.

`@eN` refs come from
`brave_snapshot` and stay valid until the page navigates.

Screenshots return a **path** rather than inline pixels: the agent reads the PNG
with whatever image

-reading tool it already has, so this plugin needs no vision
pipeline of its own.
## Requirements

1. **Brave started with a CDP port.** Add the flag to the launcher's flag file
(`~/.config/brave-fla
gs.conf` for the Arch `brave-bin` wrapper):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The flag applies at startup only, so Brave must be restarted after adding it.
The port binds to loop
back, but see Security before enabling it.

2. **Node ≥ 22** for the CLI (it uses the built-in `fetch` and `WebSocket`; no
dependencies). Node ≥
22 is also required by DSH itself.

3. **DSH** with the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` peer
packages (present i
n any DSH install) for the tool surface.

The CLI itself is bundled at `bin/brave-cdp.mjs`; the tools resolve it from the
package, falling bac

k to `~/.local/bin/brave-cdp`, then to `cliPath` /
`BRAVE_CDP_CLI`.

## CLI
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Global flags: `--tab <n|id|url-substr>`, `--json`, `--timeout <ms>`, `--port <n>`.
Env: `BRAVE_CDP_P
ORT` (9222), `BRAVE_CDP_HOST` (127.0.0.1), `BRAVE_CDP_TIMEOUT`.
`brave-cdp help` is the source of truth.
## Configuration
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `cliPath` | packaged `bin/brave-cdp.mjs` | CLI to invoke |
| `port` | `9222` | CDP port (must matc

h the Brave flag) |
| `timeoutMs` | `60000` | Per-call timeout |
| `screenshotTimeoutMs` | `120000`
| Screenshot timeout |

The bundled patch mounts the row as `brave-cdp`; a profile's own
`cordis.patch.yml` is applied after

wards, so override that id to change the port
or point at another CLI:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Security

CDP is **full control of the browser**: page contents, cookies, and any session
you are logged into

are readable, and it can act as you on any site. The port
binds to loopback only, which limits it to

local processes — that is a boundary,
not a guarantee. Add the flag when you want an agent to drive

the browser, and
remove it (and restart) when you do not.

| `bin/brave-cdp.mj

| `cordis.patch.ym

l` | the bundle patch that mounts the tools row |
| `test/` | CLI behaviour and packaging invariants

Because the CDP client lives in the CLI, the plugin is a thin adapter: one tested
code path serves b

oth the tool surface and the shell, and the DSH host process
never imports a browser-automation depe
